entries.effect: the index path it was asked about: the base layout has no opinion about where an item at that point would land, and the collection view asks its delegate after this, so a layout that arranges its items otherwise answers something else and that stands, and a delegate still has the last word

entries.effect: nil: the base layout has no attributes of its own, so it has none to move and none to give; UICollectionViewFlowLayout, which has them, places the item at the point with no size and above every other element

entries.effect: a cell with no size whose centre is the point the item is being dragged to and whose zIndex is NSIntegerMax, so the item follows the finger and is never behind another element; the size is the point's own and not the cell's laid out size, because the cell is being carried by the finger rather than placed in the grid
entries.source: the host's own UIKit under Mac Catalyst (macOS 27.0), held against the backport by tests/backports/host/collectionmovement (flow.movingAttributes.*, where the base layout's answer is nil)
